We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We have applied first two templates successfully, got precursors. Need to continue applying remaining templates sequentially to generate a chain of 5 steps ending in starting materials (maybe simple). We need to construct JSON route with each reaction node having children precursors (which may be further reactions). Must ensure each step uses the specified template ID.

We need to find for each intermediate product, a matching template. We have template IDs; we need to check applicability and apply to get precursors.

We have applied 29646 to target, got three possible precursors (list of three SMILES). We need to choose one that can be further processed with template 1914389. We applied 1914389 to one of those (the first one) and got two precursors: a complex silyl-protected molecule and an ester? Actually result: (('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C', 'CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC'),). So two precursors: precursor A (silyl protected) and precursor B (some ester). The template likely splits the molecule into two fragments.

Now next template is 1914390. We need to apply it to one of the precursors from previous step? The order likely means each step uses the template on the product of previous step. So after applying 1914389, we have two fragments; each may be further retrosynthesized using next templates. But we need a linear route of 5 steps, maybe each step transforms a single molecule (not branching). However the example shows reaction node with multiple children (reactants). So we can have branching. The requirement: route must have at least 5 reactions. Using templates in order. Could be that each reaction uses the next template on one of the fragments, while other fragments are considered final (buyable). So we need to apply 1914390 to one of the fragments (likely the silyl-protected one). Let's test applicability.

Check 1914390 on the silyl-protected SMILES: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C". We already checked and got False. So not applicable.

Maybe we should have chosen a different precursor from first template that matches 1914389? The first template gave three options; we used the first. Let's see other options.

The result from first apply_template gave three SMILES: 
1) 'C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C'
2) 'C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO'
3) 'C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO'

We applied 1914389 to the first (with two silyl groups). Maybe 1914389 works on the second (without silyl on side chain). Let's test.
